questions.q: Why does an S3 bucket name have to be unique across all of AWS, not just within your own account?
options: Because bucket names form part of a predictable URL, and two different customers can't both claim the same name
Bucket names only need to be unique within a single Region, not globally
Bucket uniqueness is only enforced for buckets created through the console, not the CLI
Because AWS limits every customer to exactly one bucket name globally
questions.explain: S3 bucket names are part of a global URL scheme like https://bucket-name.s3.amazonaws.com, so the namespace is shared by every AWS customer worldwide.

questions.q: What is an S3 object's "key," and why can it look like a folder path even though S3 has no real folder hierarchy?
options: The string that identifies the object, such as invoices/2026/summary.pdf — the slashes are just characters that the console displays as folders
The storage class assigned to the object
A checksum used to verify the object wasn't corrupted
A secret access credential required to read the object
questions.explain: S3's namespace under a bucket is flat; every object sits directly in the bucket addressed by its full key, and the console only renders slashes as folders for convenience.

questions.q: What's the real tradeoff S3 Standard-IA makes compared to S3 Standard?
options: Lower storage cost with no retrieval fee at all, identical in every other way to Standard
Standard-IA removes the millisecond retrieval guarantee entirely
Higher storage cost in exchange for faster retrieval than Standard
Lower storage cost and still millisecond retrieval, but a per-GB retrieval fee is charged whenever the object is actually read
questions.explain: Standard-IA is cheaper to store than Standard but charges a per-GB retrieval fee, so it fits data you need fast if accessed, but rarely is.

questions.q: What is the real cost of choosing S3 Glacier for an object's storage class?
options: Retrieval can take minutes to hours depending on the retrieval tier, in exchange for the lowest storage cost
Glacier objects can only be read once and are then automatically deleted
There is no tradeoff — Glacier is cheaper with the same millisecond retrieval as Standard
Glacier requires the object to be stored in a different AWS account
questions.explain: Glacier trades retrieval speed for the lowest possible storage cost — data becomes available only after a retrieval delay measured in minutes to hours.

questions.q: Which AWS CLI command creates a new S3 bucket in a specific Region?
options: aws iam create-bucket --name <name>
aws s3api create-bucket --bucket <name> --region <region>
aws s3 mb --storage-class GLACIER
aws ec2 create-volume --bucket <name>
questions.explain: aws s3api create-bucket with --bucket and --region creates a new bucket in the chosen Region, where its data physically stays.
